items.question: Which is correct? 'I enjoy ___.'
items.explanation: <Enjoy> siempre va seguido del gerundio (forma -ing): enjoy swimming.

items.question: After prepositions (in, at, of, about), we use:
items.explanation: Después de una preposición, siempre se usa el <gerund>: interested in learning, good at cooking.

items.question: Which group of verbs takes the gerund (-ing)?
items.explanation: <Enjoy>, <avoid> y <mind> van todos seguidos del gerundio (forma -ing).

items.question: "I am happy," she said. → She said she ___ happy.
items.explanation: Regla de backshift: presente simple 'am' → pasado simple 'was'.

items.question: "I have seen that film," he said. → He said he ___ that film.
items.explanation: Backshift: presente perfecto 'have seen' → pasado perfecto 'had seen'.

items.question: "Don't run!" → He told the children ___ run.
items.explanation: Órdenes negativas en estilo indirecto: told + objeto + not to + verbo base.

items.question: You're coming tonight, ___?
items.explanation: Forma positiva 'are' → coletilla negativa 'aren't you'. Se usa el mismo auxiliar invirtiendo la polaridad.

items.question: Let's have lunch, ___?
items.explanation: Regla especial: 'Let's' siempre lleva 'shall we' como coletilla.

items.question: We ought to help, ___?
items.explanation: 'Ought to' → la coletilla es 'shouldn't we' (más común que 'oughtn't we').

items.question: What is a <round-trip ticket>?
options: a ticket to go and return
items.correct: a ticket to go and return
items.explanation: Un <round-trip ticket> te permite viajar a un destino y regresar.

items.question: What does <all-inclusive> mean for a hotel?
items.explanation: <All-inclusive> significa que todas las comidas, bebidas y actividades están incluidas en el precio.

items.question: What is <backpacking>?
items.explanation: <Backpacking> es viajar de forma económica, generalmente alojándose en hostales y llevando tus pertenencias en una mochila.

items.question: What does <break the ice> mean?
items.explanation: Este modismo significa iniciar una conversación en una situación social.

items.question: What does <cost an arm and a leg> mean?
items.explanation: Este modismo significa que algo es extremadamente caro.

items.question: If something is <a blessing in disguise>, it:
options: seems bad but is actually good
items.correct: seems bad but is actually good
items.explanation: Este modismo describe algo que al principio parece malo pero termina siendo bueno.

items.question: Complete: 'If you can't sleep, try ___ some warm milk.'
items.explanation: <Try> + gerundio = experimentar con una solución. Probar a beber leche como remedio.

items.question: Which verb changes meaning depending on whether it's followed by gerund or infinitive?
items.explanation: <Stop> cambia de significado: stop doing (dejar de hacer) frente a stop to do (pausar con un propósito). Enjoy y want solo admiten una forma cada uno.

items.question: Complete: 'After living in Japan for two years, she ___ eating with chopsticks.'
items.explanation: <Be used to> + la forma en -ing expresa estar acostumbrado a algo en el presente.

items.question: Which phrasal verb means "to delay or postpone"?
items.explanation: <Put off> significa posponer o aplazar algo para más tarde.

items.question: What does <back to square one> mean?
items.explanation: Este modismo significa volver al punto de partida después de un intento fallido.

items.question: Not only ___ the exam, but he also got the highest score.
items.explanation: Not only requiere inversión: Not only + auxiliar + sujeto + verbo.

items.question: Never before ___ such a beautiful sunset.
items.explanation: Never requiere inversión: Never + auxiliar + sujeto + verbo.

items.question: Which advanced conditional is correct?
options: Were it not for his help, I would have failed
Not were it for his help, I would have failed
If it not were for his help, I would have failed
Was it not for his help, I would have failed
items.correct: Were it not for his help, I would have failed
items.explanation: Condicional invertida formal: <Were it not for> reemplaza a <If it were not for>.

items.question: Which phrasal verb means "to include something in a calculation or plan"?
items.explanation: <Factor in> significa incluir un elemento en particular al hacer un cálculo o tomar una decisión.

items.question: If someone <barks up the wrong tree>, they:
items.explanation: Este modismo significa hacer una suposición equivocada o seguir una pista falsa.

items.question: Which sentence correctly uses <scarcely ... when> to express immediacy?
options: Scarcely the proposal had been submitted when objections arose.
Scarcely had the proposal been submitted when objections arose.
Scarcely had the proposal been submitted than objections arose.
Scarcely the proposal was submitted when objections arose.
items.correct: Scarcely had the proposal been submitted when objections arose.
items.explanation: <Scarcely ... when> provoca inversión (<had the proposal been>) y se combina con <when>, no con <than> (que sigue a <no sooner>).

items.question: Choose the correct use of the mandative subjunctive in formal writing:
options: The board proposed that the CEO resign immediately.
The board proposed that the CEO resigns immediately.
The board proposed that the CEO resigned immediately.
The board proposed that the CEO has resigned immediately.
items.correct: The board proposed that the CEO resign immediately.
items.explanation: Los verbos de propuesta (<propose>, <recommend>, <move>) activan el subjuntivo mandativo: forma base <resign>, no <resigns> ni <resigned>.

items.question: When is <albeit> used?
options: to reject an idea, overall speaking
items.explanation: <Albeit> significa aunque, e introduce una concesión.

items.question: If a researcher <delves into> a topic, they:
options: Investigate or study it thoroughly and in depth
items.correct: Investigate or study it thoroughly and in depth
items.explanation: Delve into significa profundizar o investigar algo con detenimiento.

items.question: What does <a moot point> mean?
items.explanation: Este modismo describe un punto que ya no es relevante o que es puramente teórico.
